## Verdict: FAIL — N-47 is fixed, but two new blockers

N-47's own-child residue is gone, CONFIRMED on the Fable probe, the six restore fixtures, the author's property and
6 200 committed removals of this seat's own generator. Every gate is green on re-run. Two new findings are blockers
under the brief's rule (3):

* **B-1:** a wrong result on an honest input. A survivor on a stated promise is not equivalent.
* **B-2:** a survivor on a stated promise is not equivalent. Without the promise, honest inputs throw.

| line | re-run (this round) | verdict | label |
|---|---|---|---|
| **N-47** (remove(insert(x)) restores the arena: own-child records) | **Fable probe** (`probe-n13.mts`, copied unchanged into `check-M0-a-06-s1/`, run on the tree): `BEFORE faces/level [ 1, 0, 0, 0, 0 ]`, `INSERT L3 ok; faces/level [ 1, 1, 1, 1, 0 ] problems []`, `REMOVE ok; faces/level [ 1, 0, 0, 0, 0 ] problems []`, digests equal at all five levels, `contentPrint restored: true`, `encode before 1241:ref\|bytes` = `encode after 1241:ref\|bytes`, and `CHUNKS after remove: [414200471,2423536301,3245550993,854880217] bytes=152`, the same single chunk as before the insert. **Restore fixtures and property** (`test/tx/restore.test.ts`, at the PR size): 7/7 green. The property tally was `{"cases":2500,"inserted":2117,"refusedInsert":383,"refusedRemove":0,"exact":2115,"rotated":0,"sharedEnd":2,"ownChildren":1119,"byLevel":[260,350,469,522,516]}`. **Own generator** (`probe-own.mts`, 2 × 4 000 cases, seeds `c × 40 503 + 7 919` and `c × 1 299 709 + 7 919`). It used zero to three bases at L0 – L3 (cross-frame or interior), targets at L1 – L4 with 2 – 4 points, 20 % closed rings, 25 % LIFO pairs and 25 % removals by a coarser batch, and every fourth removal ran through `suiteEnv`. Over 6 200 committed removals: `facesDiff 0`, `invalid 0` (`allProblems` and `checkIndexState`), `recordBad 0` (each covered level's live-record drop equals `removed − created`), `lifoBad 0` over 859 LIFO pairs, `refusedRemove 0`. **The record:** the L1-batch fixture lists `faces[L1].removed` and `faces[L2].removed` of length 1 each. An L3 batch lists levels 3 – 4 only, which is §3.3's "the dirty set, per level ≥ the batch's level" (ARCHITECTURE line 4493), as C-0219 (3) states. **Mutants on the fix:** K01 – K04, K07, K08, K10 and K11 were killed (table below). | **FIXED** | CONFIRMED |
| **B-1** (new: remove(insert(x)) leaves a crossing vertex undissolved; M18 is not equivalent) | **Minimal repro** (`repro-vertex.mts`, on the tree): `framed()`; an L3 `plot_line` `base:0` (0,3630)–(1807,2567)–(4000,1554); then an L3 chain `x:1` (4000,3213)–(2529,2056)–(1905,2653)–(2805,1434), which crosses `base:0` twice; then `removeEdges` on `x:1` in a later L3 batch. Output: `remove ok=true problems=[]`, `print restored false \| chunk refs restored false \| L3 digest restored false`, `residue v 2052,2453 L3 f4 []`. The vertex left behind has degree 2, the `split` flag, no row, no pin, and two `base:0` edges at L3 with identical rows. That is exactly what §2.2's dissolution rule dissolves ("dissolve each vertex left with degree 2 that carries the split flag, no vertex role and no pin, and whose two remaining edges carry identical role sets and one birth level"). The own generator shows it on 4 of 6 200 removals (cases 496 and 2563 at ×40 503; cases 2619 and 3946 at ×1 299 709). None carries `W_STRETCH_SHARED`. Each is a chain crossing one run twice, and in each the encoded chunks and the level digest change. **Mechanism** (case 496, traced): the crossings (2881,1705) and (2486,1899) split `base:2`'s edge (1882,2197)–(4000,1155). `dissolve` runs in canonical (y, x) order, so (2881,1705) dissolves first. The far ends of (2486,1899) become (1882,2197) and (4000,1155), and C-0185 (4)'s `onRun` then measures 1796 / √5 571 688 = 0.76 cm > 0.71 cm. The vertex was placed within the hot pixel of the piece it split, not of the original edge, so it stays. Against its neighbours before the first merge it is on-run (0.48 cm). **M18** (dissolve without `onRun`) restores all four cases: the own generator gives `refsDiff 0`, `invalid 0` on both seed sets. M18 SURVIVES the tx folder (181/181) and `vitest related` at 1000 (only the two PENDING-S6 reds below). C-0189 (6) and N-8 call it "PLAUSIBLE equivalent"; that is refuted. It changes committed outputs on honest inputs, and the tree's code is the variant that breaks §2.2. | **FAIL (blocker)** | CONFIRMED |
| **B-2** (new: C-0219 (1)'s "listed … with their keys" for freed ancestors is untested; K09 survives) | **K09** deletes `t.log.removedKeys.set(…)` for a freed ancestor. It SURVIVES the tx folder (181/181) and `vitest related` at 1000 in the mirror (`Tests 2 failed \| 2591 passed`, the two failures being the PENDING-S6 agreements, with 0 occurrences of the key error). The fixtures never free two records at one level the record covers, so `dirtyFaces`' key sort never compares an ancestor. On honest inputs the own generator kills it at once, with the same error on both seed sets: `Error: tx: a removed record's key was kept by the writer that removed it … at tx.ts:234 … at Array.sort`. A concrete case: own case 52 at ×40 503. It is `framed()`; an L0 `way` `base:0` (1954,3576)–(3517,2133)–(3248,217); an L1 `way` `base:1` (1005,0)–(3238,2216)–(649,4000); an L4 `plot_line` `x:1` (583,2808)–(3144,1247); and `removeEdges` on `x:1` in an **L0** batch. On the tree, that record lists `faces[L2].removed` and `faces[L3].removed` of length 2 each. Not equivalent: the promise is what keeps that record from throwing. | **FAIL (blocker)** | CONFIRMED |

### Required changes (to the author, lane `build/M0-a-06-fix-s2` or the session's naming)

* **B-1.** Make the dissolution restore every crossing of one run, whatever its order. One reading that fits C-0185
  (4): decide `onRun` for every split candidate against its neighbours before the batch's first merge, or against the
  run as it stood before the batch, then merge. Another: dissolve in an order that undoes the splits. Pin it with
  `repro-vertex.mts`'s arena and cases 496, 2563, 2619 and 3946 as fixtures (contentPrint, chunk refs and the level
  digest equal to the pre-insert state). Widen `restore.test.ts`'s property generator so it would have caught this:
  3-segment chains, bases at L3, removals by a coarser batch. Then make M18 red on a fixture of the case C-0185 (4)
  exists for (a chain's own corner that carries the split flag) — or, if rule 3 (b) already clears that corner's flag
  so `onRun` in `dissolve` is redundant, record that as a CONFIRMED equivalence in the choices row.
* **B-2.** A fixture in which a batch coarser than the chain frees an own-child ancestor beside another record at a
  level the record covers. Own case 52 above works. Assert the record's `removed` lists for that level, in key order.
  K09 must go red.

## Probes and notes outside the blockers (rows in `checks/M0-a-06-notes.md`)

* **N-10** (the session, owner M0-a-14, now). C-0219 (2) is CONFIRMED and is larger than "blocks the remove path"
  suggests. With `suiteEnv` wired, 323 of 776 and 321 of 752 removals were refused with `index-freshness: an L# batch
  wrote the L# index (delete of face # (L#)) outside its promotions and demotions`. That is about 42 %. Every refusal
  left the arena unchanged, so it fails safe. Any suite-wired remove path (N-46 (6) (e), M0-a-05 S6's lifecycle cases)
  will meet it.
* **N-11** (the session). The shared-stretch end (C-0219 (4)) is CONFIRMED on the author's cases 1630 and 2337. The
  base run keeps the stretch's end vertices (1630: (271,330) and (523,1158) on L0 `base:0`), and the level digests
  differ (1630: all five; 2337: L1 – L4). §2.2 rule 3 (b) sanctions it in its own words ("where a quay left the old
  shore stretch it shared, that point becomes a shape vertex of the quay"), which conflicts with N-46 (6) (e). This is
  not M0-a-06's defect.
* **N-12** (M4). The equivalent and hardening survivors K05, K06, K12 – K16.
* **N-13** (M4). The restore property's generator is narrow: at most two segments per chain, bases at L0 – L2 only,
  and removal at the chain's own level. B-1's fix round widens it; this note records why the property missed B-1.
* **N-14** (owner of `io/roundtrip.test.ts`). The default-mix round trip runs near its 5 000 ms default timeout and
  timed out under load. Informative only.
* **N-15** (the session). N-8's deferral of M18 to M4 is superseded by B-1.
